topics.title: Vectors
topics.subject: mathematics
outcomes: describe position vectors geometrically and as column vectors (k u)
find the vector of a directed line segment when position vectors of the end points are known. (u)
find the position vector of the mid-point of a line segment. (u)
use vector method to divide a line proportionately internally and externally. (u s)
use vectors to show parallelism. (u s)
use vector methods to show co-linearity. (u s)

body.text: A boda boda rider in Mbale rides 3 km east, then 2 km north. The trip has a size and a direction, so it is a vector. In this topic you will use vectors to describe positions, find midpoints, divide lines and test whether points lie on one line.
Position vectors

Choose a fixed point O, called the origin. The position vector of a point A is the vector from O to A. We write it as OA with an arrow on top, or as a small bold letter a. On a coordinate grid, the position vector of A(3, 2) is a column vector with 3 on top and 2 below.

body.speech: vector O A equals a, which is the column vector 3, 2

body.text: On the grid, a position vector is an arrow from O to the point. The top number is the movement along the x-axis and the bottom number is the movement along the y-axis. A negative number means left or down. Below, we write column vectors across the line, like (3, 2), to save space.
The vector of a directed line segment
A directed line segment is a line from one point to another, with a direction. To go from A to B, go from A back to O, which is minus a, then from O to B, which is b.

body.speech: vector A B equals b minus a

body.text: In words: the position vector of the end point minus the position vector of the start point.
The midpoint of a line segment
The midpoint M of AB is the point halfway from A to B. Its position vector is the average of a and b.

body.speech: m equals one half of, a plus b

body.title: Find the vector AB and the midpoint of AB
steps: A is the point (1, 7) and B is the point (−3, −3), so a = (1, 7) and b = (−3, −3).
The midpoint of AB is the point (−1, 2).

body.text: Dividing a line in a given ratio
A point P divides AB internally in the ratio m : n when P lies between A and B and AP : PB = m : n. Think of the journey from A to B cut into m + n equal parts. P is m parts along.

body.speech: p equals n a plus m b, all over m plus n

body.text: A point P divides AB externally in the ratio m : n when P lies on the line AB extended, outside the segment, and AP : PB = m : n. For external division the formula has a minus sign.

body.speech: p equals m b minus n a, all over m minus n

body.title: Find B when a point divides AB internally
steps: The point P(1, 1) divides AB internally in the ratio 3 : 4. A is the point (−2, 7). Find B.
Here m = 3 and n = 4, so p = (4a + 3b) ÷ 7, which gives 7p = 4a + 3b.
Check: AP = p − a = (3, −6) and PB = b − p = (4, −8), which are 3 and 4 lots of (1, −2).

body.title: Divide a line externally
steps: A is (2, 1) and B is (5, 7). Find the point P that divides AB externally in the ratio 2 : 1.
Here m = 2 and n = 1, so p = (2b − a) ÷ (2 − 1) = 2b − a.
P is the point (8, 13).
Check: AP = (6, 12) is twice BP = (3, 6), and P lies beyond B.

body.text: Parallel vectors

Two vectors are parallel when one is a number multiple of the other. If u = kv for some number k, they lie in the same direction; if k is negative, they point opposite ways. For example, (−6, 9) = −3 × (2, −3), so these vectors are parallel.
Showing that points are collinear

Points are collinear when they lie on one straight line. To show that A, B and C are collinear, show two things. First, AB is a multiple of AC, so the two lines are parallel. Second, AB and AC share the point A, so they cannot be two separate parallel lines.

body.title: Are three boda boda stages on one straight road?
steps: On a town map, three stages are at P(1, 2), Q(3, 5) and R(7, 11).
PR = 3 × (2, 3), so PR = 3PQ. The vectors are parallel.
Both start at P, so P, Q and R lie on one straight line.

body.text: Now test A(5, 2), B(−3, 6) and C(9, 4). AB = (−8, 4) and AC = (4, 2). For a multiple, the same number must multiply both parts. But −8 ÷ 4 = −2 while 4 ÷ 2 = 2, so these points are not collinear.

body.title: Vectors on the classroom floor
body.text: Mark an origin with chalk in one corner of the classroom floor, draw axes along two walls, and mark every metre. Two learners stand at A(1, 4) and B(5, 2). The class writes down a, b and AB. A third learner walks to the midpoint given by ½(a + b). Repeat for the point dividing AB in the ratio 1 : 3.
A learner says, “If AB is parallel to CD, then A, B, C and D must all lie on one line.” When is this true, and when is it false? Draw some cases on squared paper to support your view.

A position vector goes from the origin to a point. The vector from A to B is b − a, and the midpoint has position vector ½(a + b). Vectors are parallel when one is a multiple of the other. Points are collinear when the vectors joining them are parallel and share a point.
